name: Pasta e Ceci
description: Brothy Roman pasta and chickpeas with tomato, rosemary, and kale.
recipeIngredient: 2 sprigs rosemary (leaves finely chopped; or 1 tsp dried)
2 cans chickpeas (15 oz, drained and rinsed)
8 oz pasta (short: ditalini, small shells, or broken spaghetti)

recipeInstructions.text: Heat olive oil in a dutch oven over medium. Add shallots and a pinch of salt and cook until soft, 4 minutes.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and red pepper flakes. Cook until fragrant, 1 minute.
Add tomato paste and cook, stirring, until it darkens to brick red, 2 minutes.
Add chickpeas and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer and cook 10 minutes. Mash about a third of the chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken the broth.
Stir in pasta and simmer, stirring often so it doesn't stick, until al dente, 10-12 minutes. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick; it should be loose, between a soup and a stew.
Stir in lacinato kale for the last 3 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Serve topped with grated parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.
The pasta keeps drinking the broth: thin leftovers with water or broth when reheating. Keeps 4 days. Swap in white beans for the chickpeas if that's what you have.
